ei.title: The World of Sports Taking Responsibility
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Stewardship of the environment has become an issue that affects almost all aspects of our lives. Consequently, individuals and organizations constantly strive to make small changes to their daily habits to build a greener environment. Individuals practice a more mindful approach to their way of living to reduce their environmental impact while organizations strive to modify their way of doing business to minimize their effect on the environment. The world of sports is no exception and it has a lot of potential to be part of the solution. Many sporting events have a negative impact on the environment because they require massive structures to host them. To draw more spectators, sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting bigger, consuming larger areas of land and requiring greater amounts of building materials for construction. Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a construction site, there is a loss of nature. Every ton of concrete and steel used in the building foundation and structure is produced, transported, poured, and put together by equipment and facilities that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere. Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms of resources are consumed to operate and maintain the facility. Every sporting event affects the environment before, during, and even after it. For example, a long-track speed skating competition can only take place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. As long as the competition is on, the track needs to be kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems while the temperature, humidity, and air quality inside the stadium also have to be maintained for optimal ice conditions. Additionally, all of the stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to travel to and from the stadium, often from other cities or even from abroad. In fact, more than 25% of the emissions generated by the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be caused by fan travel and accommodations. During the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they consumed leave trash cans overflowing. After the event has ended, in addition to the significant amount of trash that needs to be disposed of, the effects those people caused and the emissions generated from their travel continue to have a lasting negative impact on air quality. Alarm bells sounded when research suggested the possibility that nearly one in every four English soccer stadiums could be partially or completely flooded in the near future due to climate change and extreme weather events. Some research even predicted that by 2050 almost half of the cities that once hosted the Winter Olympics would not be able to do so again for lack of snow and ice. Also, the US Open Tennis Championships organizers implemented an “extreme heat policy,” having mandatory short breaks for players to cool down during matches, after a few quit their matches due to extreme heat. As more sports are affected by climate change, concerns are growing. There is light at the end of the tunnel, however. The sports community is optimistic that it can reduce its environmental impact by taking two main steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations before, during, and after events and raising awareness among the public about their impact. Efforts to adopt more responsible approaches have been made by various organizations, and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a good example. The IOC set up the Sport and Environment Commission decades ago and declared the environment as essential to the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and culture. It has since encouraged host nations to adopt more environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics. As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000 Sydney Summer Olympics became the world’s largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy recycling system which used the curling hall’s air conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms in the venue. Also, for the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating venue was built with salvaged timber. The Olympic Park for the 2012 London Summer Olympics, which was built on industrial land that was once contaminated, was converted to the biggest urban park in Europe. Then at the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics, electricity was generated with hydrogen instead of fossil fuel, which supplied power for many residential buildings in the Olympic Village and Paralympic Village. Thanks to its popularity, sports is a powerful tool for universally raising awareness about environmental responsibility. Simply put, the sports industry influences billions of individuals that are involved in sports either as spectators, athletes, or organizers. Through sports, strategies to increase awareness and educate the public about the importance of sustaining the environment have shown good results. Research has found that fans are receptive to ecological or environmental initiatives organized at sporting events, and many are willing to change their lifestyle habits accordingly. The social status of athletes can have a strong effect, too. For example, high-profile athletes and coaches can be sports ambassadors to foster environmental consciousness among fans, especially young people who look up to them. The broad appeal of sports becomes a vehicle to reach many people at once. While sports provide us with such immense benefits, we ─ along with sporting event organizers ─need to be aware of the adverse environmental effects that sports have at times. As long as we are all aware of the effects, we can take steps toward finding ways to minimize or even completely eliminate them. While Green Sports Day, on October 6th, is a global event that promotes environmentally friendly sports, maybe it’s time we declare every day a day to encourage greater sustainability in sports. World Link Bioremediation A Sustainable Solution to Ocean Pollution On April 20, 2010, an enormous explosion shook the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf of Mexico, causing a significant oil leak into the sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134 million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200 Olympic swimming pools, flowed into the sea before it was eventually halted. Despite continuing restoration efforts, the sea has not yet fully recovered. One approach to addressing the issue of oil contamination is bioremediation, a restoration method that utilizes bacteria. Some types of bacteria naturally exist in marine environments and possess the capability to break down various components of oil. When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are attracted to the oil and begin to multiply. As they grow, they release enzymes that break down oil into carbon dioxide and water. Although this process may take several weeks or months, it represents a more sustainable method of cleaning up oil spills compared to conventional approaches involving harmful chemicals. Bacteria can also play a role in the process of plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the ocean, some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to their growth and reproduction. Similar to the process of breaking down oil, the bacteria release enzymes that break down plastic into smaller molecules, ultimately resulting in carbon dioxide and water. It’s not all good news, however. There are challenges associated with bioremediation. The breakdown of oil or plastic by bacteria, as mentioned earlier, can be a time-consuming process requiring weeks or months. These bacteria can also be sensitive to specific environmental conditions such as temperature and sea water constituents. Despite these challenges, there is no doubt that bioremediation holds promise as a technology for oil spill or plastic cleanup in the ocean. Because the bacteria used in this process occur naturally, they do not need to be transported to the polluted site. Bioremediation may be a more effective way to confront contamination problems and reduce environmental harm.

questions.passage: Stewardship of the environment has become an issue that affects almost all aspects of our lives. Consequently, individuals and organizations constantly strive to make small changes to their daily habits to build a (A)[greener / dirtier] environment. Individuals practice a more mindful approach to their way of living to (B)[reduce / increase] their environmental impact while organizations strive to modify their way of doing business to (C)[minimize / maximize] their effect on the environment. The world of sports is no exception and it has a lot of potential to be part of the solution. Many sporting events have a negative impact on the environment because they require massive structures to host them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ (A) greener(더 친환경적인): 개인과 조직이 '더 친환경적인(greener)' 환경을 만들려 애쓴다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ dirtier(더 더러운): 환경을 좋게 만든다는 흐름과 정반대
✅ (B) reduce(줄이다): 개인은 자신의 환경 영향을 '줄이려(reduce)' 한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ increase(늘리다): 영향을 줄인다는 흐름과 반대
✅ (C) minimize(최소화하다): 조직은 환경에 미치는 영향을 '최소화하려(minimize)' 한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ maximize(최대화하다): 영향을 줄인다는 흐름과 반대
det.tip: greener=더 친환경적인, reduce=줄이다, minimize=최소화하다

questions.passage: Many sporting events have a (A)[negative / positive] impact on the environment because they require massive structures to host them. To draw more spectators, sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting (B)[bigger / smaller], consuming larger areas of land and requiring greater amounts of building materials for construction. Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a construction site, there is a (C)[loss / gain] of nature. Every ton of concrete and steel used in the building foundation and structure is produced, transported, poured, and put together by equipment and facilities that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere. Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms of resources are consumed to operate and maintain the facility.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ smaller(더 작은): 경기장이 커진다는 뒷 내용과 반대
❌ positive(긍정적인): 환경에 해를 끼친다는 문맥과 반대
✅ (A) negative(부정적인) (B) bigger(더 큰) (C) loss(손실): 많은 스포츠 행사가 환경에 '부정적(negative)' 영향을 주고, 경기장이 점점 '더 커지며(bigger)', 초지를 밀면 자연의 '손실(loss)'이 생긴다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ gain(이득): 자연이 사라진다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: negative=부정적인, bigger=더 큰, loss=손실

questions.passage: For example, a long-track speed skating competition can only take place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. As long as the competition is on, the track needs to be kept frozen by (A)[specialized / ordinary] refrigeration systems while the temperature, humidity, and air quality inside the stadium also have to be maintained for (B)[optimal / poor] ice conditions. Additionally, all of the stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to travel to and from the stadium, often from other cities or even from abroad. In fact, more than 25% of the emissions generated by the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be (C)[caused / prevented] by fan travel and accommodations. During the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they consumed leave trash cans overflowing.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ordinary(평범한): 얼음을 얼리려면 '전문(specialized)' 냉각 장치가 필요하다는 문맥과 맞지 않음
✅ (A) specialized(전문적인) (B) optimal(최적의) (C) caused(야기된): 트랙을 얼리려면 '전문(specialized)' 냉각 시스템이 필요하고, '최적의(optimal)' 얼음 상태를 유지해야 하며, 배출량 상당수가 팬 이동으로 '야기됐다(caused)'는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ poor(형편없는): 최적의 얼음 상태를 유지한다는 문맥과 반대
❌ prevented(막아진): 배출이 팬 이동으로 발생했다는 흐름과 반대
det.tip: specialized=전문적인, optimal=최적의, caused=야기된

questions.passage: To draw more spectators, sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting bigger, consuming ①<u>larger</u> areas of land and requiring greater amounts of building materials for construction.  Whenever a hectare of grassland is ②<u>cleared</u> for a construction site, there is a loss of nature.  Every ton of concrete and steel used in the building foundation and structure is produced, transported, poured, and put together by equipment and facilities that ③<u>absorb</u> waste into the ground and atmosphere.  Then, after the stadium is ④<u>completed</u>, large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms of resources are consumed to operate and maintain the facility.  Every sporting event affects the environment before, during, and even after it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ absorb → emit: 장비와 시설이 폐기물을 배출한다(emit)
det.analysis:
✅ ① larger: 경기장이 커지며 '더 넓은(larger)' 땅을 소비한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② cleared: 경기장 건설을 위해 초지가 '개간된다(cleared)'는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ absorb(흡수하다) → emit(배출하다): 콘크리트와 강철을 다루는 장비와 시설이 땅과 대기로 폐기물을 '배출한다'는 문맥이므로 emit가 맞음. 흡수한다는 정반대라 부적절 ← 정답
✅ ④ completed: 경기장이 '완공된(completed)' 뒤 자원이 소비된다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: emit(배출하다) ↔ absorb(흡수하다)

questions.passage: Additionally, all of the stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to ①<u>travel</u> to and from the stadium, often from other cities or even from abroad.  In fact, more than 25% of the emissions generated by the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be caused by fan travel and accommodations.  During the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they consumed leave trash cans ②<u>empty</u>.  After the event has ended, in addition to the ③<u>significant</u> amount of trash that needs to be ④<u>disposed</u> of, the effects those people caused and the emissions generated from their travel continue to have a lasting negative impact on air quality.  Alarm bells sounded when research suggested the possibility that nearly one in every four English soccer stadiums could be partially or completely flooded in the near future due to climate change and extreme weather events.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① travel: 직원·선수·관중이 경기장으로 '이동해야(travel)' 한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② empty(텅 빈) → overflowing(넘쳐흐르는): 관중과 선수가 먹고 마시면서 남긴 플라스틱 병과 포장지가 쓰레기통을 '넘쳐흐르게(overflowing)' 한다는 문맥이므로 overflowing이 맞음. 텅 비었다는 정반대라 부적절 ← 정답
✅ ③ significant: 처리해야 할 '상당한(significant)' 양의 쓰레기라는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ disposed: 그 쓰레기가 '처리되어야(disposed of)' 한다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: overflowing(넘쳐흐르는) ↔ empty(텅 빈)

questions.passage: Alarm bells sounded when research suggested the possibility that nearly one in every four English soccer stadiums could be partially or completely ①<u>flooded</u> in the near future due to climate change and extreme weather events.  Some research even predicted that by 2050 almost half of the cities that once hosted the Winter Olympics would not be able to do so again for ②<u>lack</u> of snow and ice.  Also, the US Open Tennis Championships organizers implemented an “extreme heat policy,” having ③<u>mandatory</u> short breaks for players to cool down during matches, after a few quit their matches due to extreme heat.  As more sports are affected by climate change, concerns are ④<u>shrinking</u>.  There is light at the end of the tunnel, however.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① flooded: 잉글랜드 축구 경기장들이 '침수될(flooded)' 수 있다는 연구 문맥에 적절
✅ ② lack: 눈과 얼음의 '부족(lack)'으로 동계 올림픽 개최가 어려워진다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ③ mandatory: 선수들에게 '의무적인(mandatory)' 휴식을 준다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ④ shrinking(줄어드는) → growing(커지는): 더 많은 스포츠가 기후변화의 영향을 받으면서 우려가 '커지고(growing)' 있다는 문맥이므로 growing이 맞음. 줄어든다는 정반대라 부적절 ← 정답
det.tip: growing(커지는) ↔ shrinking(줄어드는)

det.analysis:

det.analysis:

❌ ④ reduce(줄이다): 의식을 키운다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: foster environmental consciousness = promote ~ = 환경 의식을 키우다

questions.passage: The social status of athletes can have a strong effect, too.  For example, high-profile athletes and coaches can be sports ambassadors to foster environmental consciousness among fans, especially young people who look up to them.  The broad appeal of sports becomes a vehicle to reach many people at once.  While sports provide us with such <u>immense</u> benefits, we ─ along with sporting event organizers ─need to be aware of the adverse environmental effects that sports have at times.  As long as we are all aware of the effects, we can take steps toward finding ways to minimize or even completely eliminate them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 immense와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① tiny(아주 작은): immense(엄청난, 막대한)의 정확한 반대말 ← 정답
❌ ② famous(유명한): 명성과 관련되어 크기의 반대가 아님
❌ ③ similar(비슷한): 크기와 무관한 의미축
❌ ④ heavy(무거운): 무게를 뜻해 크기의 반대는 아님(함정)
det.tip: immense(엄청난) ↔ tiny(아주 작은)

questions.passage: The sports community is optimistic that it can reduce its environmental impact by taking two main steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations before, during, and after events and raising awareness among the public about their impact.  Efforts to adopt more <u>responsible</u> approaches have been made by various organizations, and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a good example.  The IOC set up the Sport and Environment Commission decades ago and declared the environment as essential to the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and culture.  It has since encouraged host nations to adopt more environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics.  As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000 Sydney Summer Olympics became the world’s largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy recycling system which used the curling hall’s air conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms in the venue.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 responsible와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① helpful(도움이 되는): 긍정적 의미라 반대말이 아님
❌ ② similar(비슷한): 태도와 무관한 의미축
✅ ③ careless(부주의한, 무책임한): responsible(책임감 있는)의 반대말로 가장 적절 ← 정답
❌ ④ frequent(잦은): 빈도와 관련되어 책임감의 반대가 아님
det.tip: responsible approaches(책임 있는 접근) ↔ careless(부주의한)

questions.passage:
(A) The organizers wanted to <u>draw</u> more spectators, so they lowered the ticket prices and invited famous athletes. Thanks to the effort, the stadium was packed on game day.
(B) In her art class, she learned how to <u>draw</u> a detailed portrait using only a pencil. Her teacher praised the realistic lines and shadows in the picture.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 draw의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) draw more spectators는 관중을 '끌어들이다'라는 뜻(뒤에 표를 싸게 하고 유명 선수를 초청했다는 단서), (B) draw a portrait는 연필로 초상화를 '그리다'라는 뜻(realistic lines, picture가 단서) ← 정답
❌ ② (A)와 (B)의 뜻이 서로 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (A)는 '비기다'가 아니라 '끌어들이다'
❌ ④ (B)는 '비기다'가 아니라 '그리다'
det.tip: draw: (A) 끌어들이다 / (B) 그리다

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who watches an activity or event, especially a sport, without taking part in it"

det.analysis:
❌ ① athlete(운동선수): 경기에 직접 참여하는 사람이라 정의와 반대
✅ ② spectator(관중): 직접 참여하지 않고 특히 스포츠 경기를 지켜보는 사람 ← 정답
❌ ③ referee(심판): 경기를 진행·판정하는 사람이라 정의와 다름
❌ ④ coach(코치): 선수를 지도하는 사람이라 정의와 다름
det.tip: spectator = 참여하지 않고 지켜보는 관중

questions.passage: Many sporting events have a negative impact on the environment because they require massive structures to host them. To draw more spectators, sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting bigger, __________ (consume) larger areas of land and requiring greater amounts of building materials for construction.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: consume(동사, 소비하다) → consuming(현재분사): 뒤의 requiring과 and로 이어지는 분사구문 자리다. 주절의 주어(stadiums and facilities)가 땅을 '소비하는' 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 -ing를 써서 consuming이 된다. 'getting bigger, consuming ~, and requiring ~'의 병렬 분사 구조다.
det.tip: and로 이어지는 분사구문 + 능동 관계 → 현재분사 consuming

questions.passage: In fact, more than 25% of the emissions __________ (generate) by the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be caused by fan travel and accommodations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: generate(동사, 발생시키다) → generated(과거분사): 명사 the emissions를 뒤에서 꾸미는 분사 자리다. 배출량은 올림픽에 의해 '발생되는' 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 generated를 써서 'the emissions (that were) generated by ~(~에 의해 발생된 배출량)'가 된다. 문장의 진짜 동사는 뒤의 are estimated이다.
det.tip: 명사(emissions) 뒤 수식 + 수동 관계 → 과거분사 generated

questions.passage: There is light at the end of the tunnel, however.  The sports community is optimistic that it can reduce its environmental impact by taking two main steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations before, during, and after events and __________ among the public about their impact.  Efforts to adopt more responsible approaches have been made by various organizations, and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a good example.  The IOC set up the Sport and Environment Commission decades ago and declared the environment as essential to the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and culture.  It has since encouraged host nations to adopt more environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① raising awareness(인식을 높이는 것): 스포츠계가 환경 영향을 줄이는 두 번째 방법으로, 대중에게 자신들의 영향에 대한 '인식을 높이는 것'이 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ② hiding information(정보를 숨기는 것): 대중에게 알린다는 긍정적 흐름과 반대
❌ ③ cutting costs(비용을 줄이는 것): 환경 인식이 아니라 비용 이야기라 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ limiting access(접근을 제한하는 것): 대중의 인식 제고와 무관
det.tip: raising awareness among the public: 대중의 인식을 높이는 것

questions.passage: There are challenges associated with bioremediation.  The breakdown of oil or plastic by bacteria, as mentioned earlier, can be a time-consuming process requiring weeks or months.  These bacteria can also be sensitive to specific environmental conditions such as temperature and sea water constituents.  Despite these challenges, there is no doubt that bioremediation __________ as a technology for oil spill or plastic cleanup in the ocean.  Because the bacteria used in this process occur naturally, they do not need to be transported to the polluted site.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① loses value(가치를 잃다): 뒤에 이어지는 긍정적 평가와 반대
❌ ② causes harm(해를 끼치다): 생물학적 정화가 환경 피해를 줄인다는 흐름과 반대
❌ ③ makes noise(소음을 내다): 문맥과 전혀 무관
✅ ④ holds promise(가능성을 지니다): 여러 어려움에도 불구하고 생물학적 정화가 해양 정화 기술로서 '가능성을 지닌다'는 것은 의심의 여지가 없다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
det.tip: holds promise as a technology: 기술로서 가능성을 지니다
